```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
library(sciparseR)
```

JATS (Journal Article Tag Suite) is the XML format used by PubMed Central
and most publishers. When a JATS version of an article exists it is the
best source: sections, tables and references are tagged by the publisher,
so nothing has to be guessed. sciparseR reads JATS into the same document
model as PDF, so all accessors, the extraction layer, validation and
exports work the same way.

```{r}
j <- sc_parse(system.file("extdata", "trial_article.xml", package = "sciparseR"))
j
```

## Metadata

```{r}
md <- sc_metadata(j)
str(md[c("title", "journal", "year", "doi", "pmid", "pmcid", "license")])
md$field_sources
```

## Structure without coordinates

JATS has no page geometry. Blocks have an XPath instead of a box, and
the coordinate columns are `NA`:

```{r}
head(sc_blocks(j)[, c("block_id", "type", "xpath")], 6)
sc_sections(j)[, c("level", "title", "label")]
```

## Tables with spans

`rowspan` and `colspan` are kept, and `<thead>` rows are header rows:

```{r}
c1 <- sc_table_cells(j, sc_tables(j)$table_id[1])
c1[c1$is_header, c("row", "col", "row_span", "col_span", "text")]
sc_table_to_dataframe(j, sc_tables(j)$table_id[1])
```

## Equations, references and citations

Display formulas keep their TeX and MathML, with
`latex_status = "source_markup"` to say the LaTeX came from the source:

```{r}
sc_equations(j)[, c("label", "latex", "latex_status")]
substr(sc_equations(j)$mathml, 1, 80)
```

References come from `<ref>` elements with their identifiers; citations
from `<xref ref-type="bibr">`, so links are exact:

```{r}
sc_references(j)[, c("ref_id", "authors", "year", "journal", "doi", "pmid")]
sc_citations(j)[, c("marker", "ref_id", "status")]
j$supplementary[, c("label", "caption", "href")]
```

## Safety

XML is read without network access and without entity substitution, so a
file cannot make the parser fetch URLs or read local files.

## Getting JATS from PubMed Central

`sc_fetch_pmc()` downloads the JATS XML of an open access article. It
contacts NCBI only when you set `allow_network = TRUE`, and by default it
refuses articles whose license is not an open license.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
f <- sc_fetch_pmc("PMC1234567", dest = tempdir(), allow_network = TRUE)
doc <- sc_parse(f)
```

## PDF and JATS of the same article

The fixture `trial_article.xml` and `trial_tables.pdf` describe the same
synthetic trial. The rules engine finds the same numbers in both:

```{r}
pdf <- sc_parse(system.file("extdata", "trial_tables.pdf", package = "sciparseR"))
hr <- function(d) {
  o <- sc_observations(sc_extract(d, "numerical_results"))
  o[which(o$statistic == "estimate" & !is.na(o$timepoint)), c("outcome", "effect_measure", "value")]
}
hr(pdf)
hr(j)
```
